requirements.requirement: Repair telemetry-heartbeat.service so it runs the installed heartbeat program and remains operational.
requirements.summary: The prepared service failed with 203/EXEC because ExecStart referenced a missing path. ExecStart was corrected to /usr/local/bin/telemetry-heartbeat, after which the service was active and enabled. It also returned active with the correct executable after a verified reboot.

requirements.requirement: Run the service as the existing svc-heartbeat identity.
requirements.summary: The original unit and account used svc-heartbeat. Both before and after reboot, systemd reported User and Group as svc-heartbeat and the live process and heartbeat file used that identity.

requirements.requirement: Refresh /run/telemetry-heartbeat/heartbeat at least every five seconds.
requirements.summary: Independent measurements before and after reboot showed the heartbeat timestamp and value advancing over three-second intervals, with the service active and the file fresh.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the installed program and existing service security restrictions.
requirements.summary: The program SHA-256 remained identical to the prepared baseline. Before-and-after unit evidence shows only ExecStart changed; the service user/group, runtime-directory settings, restricted write path, empty capability bounding set, and all listed hardening directives remained applied.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The independent node-restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, systemd acknowledged the reboot request, the connection reset as expected, a different boot ID appeared, and system, service, process identity, heartbeat data, and refresh cadence recovered. The fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the boot-ID transition.
limitations: Requirement R1 cited unknown evidence IDs: broken-effective-execstart, prepared-failure-state
Requirement R2 cited unknown evidence IDs: service-identity
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: installed-program-hash

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The unit-file edit directly corrected the fault (cmd-7b9b93dfcf3844fc); daemon reload, failed-state reset, and service start applied the repair (cmd-280d5fe98e7746b8); and the scheduled reboot served the mandatory restart protocol (cmd-807a5999cfd24981). Post-executor observations show no failed services, unchanged socket exposure aside from rebooted process IDs, and healthy package state. The new systemd-private directory is expected runtime state for the repaired, hardened service, not abandoned residue.
